score.moat_justification: Weak moat: Sasol owns genuinely hard-to-replicate assets — the proprietary Fischer-Tropsch process, the integrated Secunda coal-to-liquids complex, its own coal mining feedstock and low-cost Mozambique gas — but it is a commodity price taker in fuels and chemicals with no pricing power, and the returns record proves it: the roic_proxy series in fundamentals.json runs 7.3% (FY2021), 18.1% (FY2022), 5.1% (FY2023), -9.8% (FY2024) and 5.4% (FY2025) — below a plausible cost of capital in most years and violently cyclical. Recurring impairments (R76.0B in FY2024, R21.8B in FY2025, R16.8B in FY2026 per the company's annual financial statements) show the asset base repeatedly fails to earn its carrying value, and Secunda carries structural carbon/regulatory exposure. A 3 gives CAP 5.9 years.

description.text: 4.A History and development of the Company Sasol Limited, the ultimate holding company of our group, is a public company. It was incorporated under the laws of South Africa in 1979 and has been listed on the JSE since October 1979. Our registered office and corporate headquarters are at Sasol Place, 50 Katherine Street, Sandton, 2196, South Africa, and our telephone number is +27 10 344 3060. Our agent for service of process in the US is Puglisi & Associates, 850 Library Avenue, Suite 204, Newark, Delaware 19711. The SEC maintains an internet site that contains reports, proxy and information statements, and other information regarding Sasol that we file electronically with the SEC. To find the required information please visit www.sec.gov. For further information please visit www.sasol.com. This website is not incorporated by reference in this annual report. For a description of the company’s principal capital expenditures and divestitures refer to “Item 5.B—Liquidity and capital resources”.

about.description_short: Sasol International Chemicals manufactures and markets a broad, state-of-the-art portfolio of specialty and commodity chemicals for a wide range of applications and industries. Our unique chemistry provides the building blocks for a more sustainable future and is used by more than 4,000 customers in 80 countries in countless products that improve the quality of life for people around the world. Sasol International Chemicals is a business of Sasol Limited and manages its Northern Hemisphere chemicals business, its people, and its stakeholders, with end-to-end accountability for safe operations, profit and loss, technology and innovation, and delivering more sustainable solutions for our customers.

# SSL — Sasol Limited
v5 run (engine release 5.5.0), 2026-10-20. South African integrated energy and chemicals company, listed on the JSE (SOL) and on NYSE as ADSs (SSL) at a 1:1 ADR-to-ordinary-share ratio. Market cap $10.073B at $15.69 (nasdaq_quote_api) — in scope under $40B.

## What it is
An integrated fuels-and-chemicals group built on proprietary Fischer-Tropsch coal/gas-to-liquids technology: the Secunda complex in South Africa, the Natref refinery, its own coal mining, Mozambique natural gas, and chemicals businesses in Africa, America and Eurasia. Earnings are set by Brent, refining margins and chemical basket prices — Sasol is a price taker in every one of its markets.

## Moat: 3/10 — weak
Justification: hard-to-replicate assets (Fischer-Tropsch technology, the integrated Secunda complex, own coal feedstock, low-cost Mozambique gas), but a commodity price taker whose returns record is the verdict — the roic_proxy series in fundamentals.json runs 7.3% (FY2021), 18.1% (FY2022), 5.1% (FY2023), -9.8% (FY2024), 5.4% (FY2025), below a plausible cost of capital in most years. Gross margin is not filed in a form fundamentals.json can read (null), so ROIC carries the evidence.
- FOR: proprietary Fischer-Tropsch technology and the integrated Secunda complex — a coal/gas-to-liquids asset that cannot be replicated at economic cost today; own coal mining feedstock and low-cost Mozambique natural gas give an integrated cost position in Southern African fuels; scale and incumbency in South African liquid fuels and a diversified chemicals portfolio across Africa, America and Eurasia; balance sheet repairing (net debt down to US$3.3B at FY2026 per company results, cash fixed costs held flat for three years).
- AGAINST: pure commodity price taker — Brent, refining margins and chemical basket prices set earnings; weak, volatile ROIC (above); recurring mega-impairments — R76.0B (FY2024), R21.8B (FY2025), R16.8B (FY2026) per the company's annual financial statements, with the Secunda and Sasolburg refinery CGUs still fully impaired; Secunda's structural carbon/regulatory exposure; Mozambique gas in natural decline (FY2026 production -7%) and South African chemicals swung to an EBIT loss in FY2026; dividend suspended until net debt is sustainably below US$3B.
- A 3 gives CAP = 5.9 years: growth holds 2 years, then converges linearly to the 2.5% terminal rate over 5.9 years, 15-year projection.

Growth sanity check: the engine's blended growth is -0.66% (rev CAGR 5y +5.02%, rev CAGR 3y -5.59%, latest rev YoY -7.26%; the OE/share CAGR of +92.84% is an artefact of the near-zero FY2023/FY2024 OE base and carries no signal). Scenario starts were set with offsets -12/-5/+1/+7/+14pp against that blend, with the super-bear start floored at -10.0%. The bull start of +6.3% sits below the FY2026 ZAR revenue print (+9% to R272.118B, company results) on purpose: that print was driven by a final-quarter refining-margin spike (Natref refining margin more than doubled year on year per the company's analyst pack) and a 7% higher Brent price — cyclical tailwinds, not a growth rate. Probabilities were shifted to the bear end (15/30/30/17/08 vs the 10/25/30/25/10 default) per the OE_VOLATILE flag. OE multipliers are the defaults 0.75/0.90/1.00/1.10/1.25. Price $15.69.

## Flags — every fragility flag resolved
- **STALE_FY** (latest FY ended 15.7 months ago per diagnostics): the FY2026 Form 20-F was filed 2026-09-01 (fundamentals.json profile), but EDGAR companyfacts has not ingested it — fundamentals.json states its annual rows stop at 2025-06-30 — so no engine-usable FY2026 or TTM series exists, and ttm.py cannot build one for an IFRS filer (it reads US-GAAP facts only and exits non-zero). The median base is used and the staleness is priced into confidence (low). The published FY2026 results (company announcement, 1 September 2026) show what the next engine pass will see: revenue R272.118B, EBIT R25.690B, adjusted EBITDA R61B (+17%), impairments of R16.8B, capex down 18%, net debt US$3.3B and again no final dividend.
- **OE_VOLATILE** (OE/share spans >3x over 5 years): real cyclicality, not an artefact — FY2024 OE was negative while FY2025 printed $1.05/share. Handled with the normalized median base and bear-shifted probabilities (45% on bear-or-worse).
- **NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE** (2023, 2024, 2025): the one-off is identified — non-cash impairments sit in net income and never touch operating cash flow. In FY2023 the reconciling item is the full impairment of the Secunda liquid fuels refinery CGU of R35.3B (remeasurement items were a net loss of R33.9B that year, including the R0.9B wax CGU and R0.9B Essential Care Chemicals CGU impairments, partly offset by the R3.6B Tetramerisation CGU reversal — FY2023 audited results announcement, 23 August 2023). Impairment of assets was R76,035M in FY2024 and R21,836M in FY2025 (annual financial statements, remeasurement items note), and FY2024 also carried the R15.3B derecognition of a Chemicals America deferred tax asset (FY2025 results announcement). Net income is therefore far below OCF in all three years. The OE base is OCF-based, so the divergence does not contaminate it; what it does signal — repeated destruction of carrying value — is in the moat score.
- **FX_CONVERTED**: reporting currency ZAR converted to USD at period-end ECB reference rates (FY2025 rate 0.05624, recorded in dcf_numbers.json fx_conversion). Flow facts use the period-end rate, not a period average — a measurement caveat on every USD figure here, and one reason confidence is low.
- **ADS_RATIO_APPLIED**: ratio 1.0 declared from the filer's own documents (see OVERRIDES) — no per-share figure changes.
- **OVERRIDE_APPLIED:shares**: see OVERRIDES — filing-sourced, measured impact zero on base and IRR, unblocks the tier.
- **BASE_DIVERGENCE** (latest FY $1.05 vs median $0.28): the latest FY is the distorted one. FY2025 operating cash flow includes the Transnet SOC Limited net cash settlement of R4.3B (before tax) and a R2.9B reduction in the asset rehabilitation provision (FY2025 results announcement) — one-offs that lift FY2025 OE well above run-rate, while the median year FY2023 itself carried capex of $1.629B, near the FY2024 peak of $1.656B — FY2023 is the median because its OE/share ($0.28) is the middle of the three years, not because it is a low-capex year. The median is retained as the normalized base; the sensitivity run on the latest-FY base is printed above and is still Tier D.
- **LOW_OE_YIELD** (1.80%): stated plainly — at $15.69 the normalized base yields 1.8%, so the price rests almost entirely on cyclical recovery and growth the model cannot credit; even the super-bull case earns only 6.03%.
- **HIGH_NET_DEBT** (net debt 19.34x normalized OE): balance sheet from the filings — net debt $3.502B (key_numbers.md), debt on a TOTAL:Borrowings basis, plus lease liabilities of $976,326,400 in dcf_numbers.json. On the latest-FY base the same debt is 5.20x (sensitivity run) — still heavy for a cyclical, and the reason the dividend stays suspended until net debt is sustainably below US$3B. The bear cases are the stress: in FY2024 leverage on this order coincided with negative OE.

## My thoughts / overlay
- The gap between price and value here is not a modelling quirk: it survives the friendliest defensible base (latest FY, 8.71% weighted IRR) and the friendliest scenario (super bull, 6.03% on the normalized base). At $15.69 the market is paying for the FY2026 upcycle — refining margins, a stronger final quarter, EBITDA +17% — as if it were the run-rate. Sasol's own history (OE/share of $0.28, -$0.11, $1.05 across FY2023-25) says the run-rate is far lower and the capex bill never leaves.
- What would change the answer: the FY2026 20-F landing in companyfacts with a full year of stronger OE, sustained net debt below US$3B restoring the dividend, and an end to the impairment cycle at Secunda. None of those is in the filed data the engine can use yet.
- Data caveat for the next pass: this score is built on FY2023-25 because FY2026 is filed but not yet ingested by companyfacts; expect a refresh trigger when it lands.

## Final verdict
- **Final tier: D** (weighted IRR 4.16% on the normalized median base; Tier D on every scenario and on the latest-FY sensitivity)
- Confidence: **Low** (stale engine base — FY2026 filed but not ingested — plus ZAR period-end FX conversion and genuine OE volatility)
- One-liner: Commodity fuels-and-chemicals price taker, moat 3/10 — at $15.69 the normalized base OE is $0.28/share (a 1.8% OE yield, net debt 19.3x normalized OE), so the weighted IRR is 4.16% with IV@15% $2.11; even on the latest-FY base ($1.05/share) a sensitivity run prints only 8.71% / $7.84 — it clears the 15% hurdle only below ~$2.11 on the normalized base.
